title: Best LGR Dehumidifier (2026): Flood & Water Damage Picks
h1: The Best LGR Dehumidifiers for Flooded Basements and Water Damage
dek: When a basement floods, a household dehumidifier stalls just as the hard part begins. Low-grain refrigerant units keep pulling water out of carpet, drywall and framing.
description: The best LGR dehumidifiers for flood damage and water restoration, from the Dri-Eaz LGR 7000XLi to the AlorAir Storm, with amp draw and drying tips.
intro: An **LGR dehumidifier** — short for low-grain refrigerant — is the machine restoration crews roll in after a burst pipe or a flooded basement. It works like an ordinary compressor dehumidifier, but it pre-cools incoming air before it reaches the coil, so it keeps wringing water out long after the room feels dry. That last stretch is where wet subfloors, wall cavities and carpet pad actually dry out.

Household dehumidifiers are built to hold a comfortable room at 50%. After a flood, you need something that can pull a space well below that and run around the clock for days. Below are the LGR units worth buying, from homeowner-friendly AlorAir models to the Dri-Eaz machines pros have relied on for years, plus how to size, power and actually use one.

items.label: AHAM test condition — the fairest number to compare
Saturation condition behind the biggest pint claims
Continuous-load limit on a standard 15-amp household circuit

blocks.text: Every LGR spec sheet quotes two capacities, and the saturation number can be nearly double the AHAM one. Saturation describes the first hours in a soaked room; AHAM is closer to the days of drying that follow. Compare machines on AHAM pints, then check the amps before you plug in more than one.

We don’t run a restoration lab. We compare manufacturer spec sheets for AHAM and saturation capacity, airflow, amp draw, pump lift and weight, and we read dealer listings and manuals for warranty and service details. Owner and contractor reviews fill in the rest: failed pumps, cracked housings, tripped breakers.

We weighted AHAM capacity and amp draw most heavily, because together they decide how much water you can remove on the circuits you actually have. Pump reliability, portability and warranty came next.

sections.heading: What to look for in an LGR dehumidifier

items.label: AHAM pints, not just saturation pints
items.text: Saturation figures flatter every machine. Use the AHAM rating to compare units and size the job.

items.label: Amp draw
items.text: A 15-amp circuit should carry no more than 12 amps continuously. That decides whether you can run two dehumidifiers — or one plus air movers — on the same circuit.

items.label: A built-in pump and enough hose
items.text: Flood dry-outs run 24/7, so a bucket is a nonstarter. Check pump lift and hose length against the distance to your nearest sink or drain.

items.label: Weight and handling
items.text: Full-size units top 100 pounds. If the loss is upstairs or down narrow steps, a compact LGR is easier to place.

items.label: Cold-weather defrost
items.text: Floods often hit unheated basements and garages. Auto-defrost keeps the unit working when the space is cool.

sections.heading: What makes an LGR different from a regular dehumidifier?

blocks.text: “Grains” refers to grains of moisture per pound of air, the unit restoration pros use to track how much water the air holds. A conventional refrigerant dehumidifier cools air over a cold coil until water condenses. As the room dries, there’s less moisture to condense, and output tapers off sharply.

An LGR adds a heat exchanger that pre-chills incoming air before it hits the coil. That extra cooling lets the coil condense water out of much drier air, so the machine keeps working when a household unit has effectively stalled. That’s the difference between air that feels dry and materials that are dry.

blocks.title: Not every heavy-duty unit is an LGR
blocks.text: Plenty of big portable units are conventional refrigerant designs with large capacities. If the listing doesn’t say low-grain refrigerant or LGR, assume it isn’t one. Our [best industrial dehumidifier](/best/best-industrial-dehumidifier/) guide covers non-LGR heavy-duty options.

sections.heading: How to dry a flooded basement with an LGR dehumidifier

items: **Make it safe.** Shut off power to the flooded area before stepping in standing water, and don’t restore it until an electrician or the utility says it’s safe.
**Remove the water.** Pump or wet-vac standing water first; a dehumidifier removes moisture from air and materials, not puddles.
**Pull out what can’t be saved.** Wet carpet pad, soaked insulation and drywall that wicked water usually come out. Carpet itself can sometimes be dried in place.
**Close the space and start drying.** Seal doors and windows, run the LGR continuously, and add air movers aimed across wet surfaces.
**Measure, don’t guess.** Track progress with a moisture meter on walls and subfloors, not just the room’s humidity reading.
**Watch the clock.** The EPA advises drying wet materials within 24–48 hours to prevent mold growth, so start as soon as the water is out.

blocks.title: When to call a pro
blocks.text: Water from sewage backups or outdoor flooding can carry contaminants. Those losses, and anything covering more than a room or two, are worth a professional restoration company — and usually an insurance call. Our guide to [whether a dehumidifier helps with mold](/guides/does-a-dehumidifier-help-with-mold/) covers the cleanup side.

For a homeowner drying out a flooded basement or recovering from a leak, the **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** is the best LGR dehumidifier for the money: real low-grain drying, a pump and a low amp draw. Step up to the **AlorAir Storm Elite** or the **Dri-Eaz LGR 7000XLi** for a whole basement, choose the **Dri-Eaz LGR 6000Li** when noise matters, and the **Dri-Eaz Revolution** for small, hard-to-reach rooms. If this is a one-time emergency, compare the cost of renting before you buy.

faqs.a: LGR stands for low-grain refrigerant. It’s a compressor dehumidifier with an extra heat exchanger that pre-cools incoming air, letting it keep removing water from air that’s already fairly dry. That’s why restoration crews use LGRs to dry out buildings after floods and leaks.

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for a flooded basement?
faqs.a: For most homeowners, the AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme, which is rated at 85 pints a day (AHAM), has a built-in pump and draws only about 5.4 amps. For a large, fully flooded basement, the AlorAir Storm Elite or Dri-Eaz LGR 7000XLi adds more capacity.

faqs.q: Is the Dri-Eaz LGR 7000XLi worth it?
faqs.a: For restoration pros and owners of multiple properties, yes: it’s rated at 130 pints a day AHAM and built to survive years of job sites. For a single homeowner’s one-time flood, an AlorAir Storm unit or a rental is usually the better value.

faqs.q: What is the amp draw of an LGR dehumidifier?
faqs.a: It varies by size. The AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme draws about 5.4 amps, the Dri-Eaz LGR 6000Li 6.5 amps, the LGR 7000XLi 8.8 amps and the LGR 3500i 10.8 amps. Keep the total on a 15-amp circuit at or below 12 amps.

faqs.q: How long should I run a dehumidifier after a flood?
faqs.a: Until a moisture meter shows walls, subfloors and framing back to normal readings, not just until the room feels dry. Small, quickly caught leaks often dry in a few days; larger losses can take a week or more.

faqs.q: Can a dehumidifier dry wet carpet?
faqs.a: It helps, especially an LGR paired with air movers blowing across the surface. Soaked carpet pad usually needs to be removed, and carpet that sat in contaminated water should be replaced.
